<reason>PRO won by turning CON's strongest dilemmas into design problems with a bounded solution: a finite, recipient-directed endowment where obligation explains why to pay but Lagos sets how to spend, plus the underfunded-not-incompetent reframe. CON's finish-line and boardroom-control case was sharp and memorable, but its always-control claim and ship-apologize-walk-away alternative never answered the survival point that return without capacity locks in the theft's second half. B also paid an execution cost for an over-limit clipped opening.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's R1/R2 answer that control is a design choice, not a law of physics — finite endowment, interest funds care, Lagos decides recipient and priorities — most directly blunted CON's autonomous-vs-obligation and perpetual-dependency attacks.</best_rebuttal>
